exec.title: Talent command view
exec.keyHint: Hover a number for headcount; click to open the list

whole.q: Are our key people staying, and is every seat covered?
whole.def: Four core numbers. Key talent: people a Supervisor named. Medium or high retention risk: medium or high ÷ key talent. Ready-now coverage: critical roles with a Ready Now successor ÷ all critical roles (TBH excluded). Career conversation gap: career goals not yet discussed ÷ key talent.
whole.value: Shows the three people risks at once: will they leave, is anyone ready, are Supervisors talking with them. Departments are flagged only when 10 points worse than the plant, so small differences don't take up time.
whole.use: Pick this quarter's focus department and topic. Click a department and every chapter below switches to it.

risk.q: Who may leave, why, and whose departure hurts most?
risk.def: Retention risk is the Supervisor's assessment (high, medium, low). Grid = risk × whether the person holds a critical role. Reason share = people with that reason ÷ medium or high risk people (several allowed).
risk.value: High risk in a critical role hurts the business the day they leave, so they come first. When reasons cluster, a policy fix works better than one-by-one retention.
risk.use: Within two weeks, the Supervisor and HRBP agree a retention action for each high-risk critical role holder; take the top two reasons to the pay or policy discussion.

bench.q: If a critical seat empties tomorrow, who steps in?
bench.def: Each critical role is classed by its best successor: ready now, 1–2 years, long term (3+ years or emergency cover), none (nobody or only TBH). Danger zone = high risk with nobody, medium risk with nobody, high risk with only long-term cover. Depth = named candidates (TBH excluded).
bench.value: Roles are compared, not people. A danger-zone role that empties means hiring outside or a long vacancy. A role with one candidate drops to zero if that person leaves.
bench.use: Name a successor or start hiring for danger-zone roles before next quarter; add a second candidate where there is only one.

growth.q: Are people getting ready, and are plans moving?
growth.def: Next-step readiness: each person's nearest. Internal pool: ready within two years and open to moving within two years. Goals counted by status (not started, on track, at risk, completed). PBM Our Values: times named as a strength or an improvement area.
growth.value: People who are ready with nowhere to go become a retention risk. Goals stuck at not started or at risk mean the review has not turned into action. Shared PBM improvement areas suit a group program.
growth.use: Check the internal pool before opening a role; find out why goals are stuck before the next checkpoint; put the top PBM improvement area into next year's training plan.

actions.q: What do we commit to this quarter?
actions.def: Each card is a list with a clear rule; click the number to open it. Rules are defined in each chapter.
actions.value: Turns the review into actions that can be assigned and tracked, not a report.
actions.use: Give each item an owner and a date, and follow up at the next management meeting.
